home.title: Tag and privacy audit
home.sub: We visit the site in a real browser, test behavior before and after consent, and show exactly where each item was observed. If we cannot observe it, we say so.
home.f1d: Network requests, cookies, dataLayer, gtag/fbq, and source code — every finding links directly to the collected evidence.
home.f2d: Three isolated contexts: without interaction, after "Reject all", and after "Accept all".
home.f3d: No simulated data, no estimated fines, no guessed scores. "Not verified" whenever applicable.

noLogin: Every claim points to the collected evidence. Running an analysis requires an account (free, no card).
phases: Opening site in a real browser
Collecting network, cookies, storage, and dataLayer

glossary.gtm: Google Tag Manager (GTM): a tool that loads and manages tags (measurement code) on a website without altering code on every change.
glossary.ga4: Google Analytics 4 (GA4): a Google tool that measures visits and actions on websites and apps.
glossary.datalayer: dataLayer: a list of information published by the site for GTM and other tools to use (for example, events and purchase values).
glossary.cmp: CMP (consent management platform): the cookie banner that records the visitor's choice.
glossary.consentmode: Consent Mode: a Google feature that adjusts tag behavior according to the visitor's consent choice.
glossary.tag: Tag: code from a measurement or advertising tool loaded on the site.
glossary.trigger: Trigger: a rule defining when a tag fires (for example, "on all pages" or "on form submission").
glossary.evidence: Evidence: the record collected during the test that supports a finding (for example, a network request).
glossary.gcs: gcs: a parameter sent by Google indicating the consent state at the time of transmission.
glossary.pixel: Pixel: tracking code used by advertising platforms, such as Meta Pixel.
glossary.measurementid: Measurement ID: the G-XXXXXXXX identifier of the GA4 property receiving the data.
